marks.gloss_en: הוה עובדא: the pomegranate died without its flower, the caper-fruit survived without its flower
there was an incident: they removed a pomegranate's flower and the pomegranate withered; they removed a caper-fruit's flower and the caper-fruit survived
ומדלגבי ערלה לאו פירא נינהו, לגבי ברכות נמי לאו פירא נינהו
(והלכתא כמר בר רב אשי דזריק את האביונות ואכיל את הקפריסין) -- bracketed in the text
since the buds are not fruit for orla, they are not fruit for blessings either: over them one says not borei pri haetz but borei pri haadama
ואזדא רבא לטעמיה, דאמר רבא: כס פלפלי ביומא דכפורי פטור -- chewing peppers is not eating
Rav Sheshet: over peppers one says shehakol
כוותיה דרב כהנא מסתברא, דרב ושמואל דאמרי תרוייהו: כל שיש בו מחמשת המינין מברכין עליו בורא מיני מזונות
Rav Yehuda: over chavitz kedera and daysa one says shehakol nihye bidvaro
רבי עקיבא במקום רבי אליעזר עבדינן כוותיה, ובית שמאי במקום בית הלל אינה משנה (= p_bs_bimkom_bh)
R' Akiva against R' Eliezer, we act as he says; Beit Shammai against Beit Hillel is no mishnah
ותיפוק ליה דנעשה שומר לפרי -- the bud protects the fruit, and 'et piryo' includes the fruit's protection, so the buds should be forbidden as orla
'you shall treat its fruit as orla' (Lev 19:23): 'et piryo' includes what is secondary to its fruit, namely the fruit's protection
אלא אמר רבא: protection is only what the fruit dies without; removing the bud does not kill the caper-fruit (= p_rava_meit_peira; his answers at 36b.4 and 36b.6 fell -- see header)
Rava (3): something is protection for the fruit only where removing it kills the fruit; here removing the bud does not
איתיביה אביי: the pomegranate's flower does not join for tumah -- מדקאמר... אלמא דלאו אוכל הוא -- yet ותנן גבי ערלה: the pomegranate's flower is liable to orla
the mishnah: a pomegranate's crown joins [it for the measure of tumah], and its flower does not
איני?! והאמר רב נחמן אמר רבה בר אבוה: orla date-coverings are forbidden as protection; ושומר לפירי אימת הוי -- בכופרא, and still he calls them protection
Rabba bar Avuh: these orla date-coverings are forbidden, since they became protection for the fruit
רב נחמן סבר לה כרבי יוסי, ופליגי רבנן עליה (= p_rn_kerabbi_yosei; itself brought down at 36b.9-10)
Rav Nachman holds like R' Yosei, and the Rabbanan dispute him -- so the date-coverings do not tell against Rava's criterion for the Rabbanan

ובשאר אילני מי פליגי רבנן עליה? והתנן... ושאר כל האילנות משיוציאו; and (36b.10) מאן שמעת ליה דאמר בוסר אין סמדר לא -- רבנן, וקתני שאר כל האילנות משיוציאו: in other trees the Rabbanan too count the earliest fruit
Beit Shammai: in the Sabbatical year one may not cut any tree from when it produces [fruit]
פול הלבן סלקא דעתך?! -- a grape is never a white bean
אלא אימא: שיעורו כפול הלבן -- its size is that of a white bean
Rav Asi: misheyegaru is the unripe grape (boser), it is the kernel, it is the white bean
מיתיבי: R' Meir counts the pepper tree as 'a tree for food', liable to orla -- so peppers are food
R' Meir: 'a tree for food' (Lev 19:23) comes to include a tree whose wood and fruit taste alike -- the pepper tree -- to teach that peppers are liable to orla
לא קשיא: הא ברטיבתא, הא ביבשתא -- R' Meir speaks of fresh peppers, Rava of dry
אמרי ליה רבנן למרימר: כס זנגבילא ביומא דכפורי פטור? והא אמר רבא: Indian himalta is permitted and one says borei pri haadama over it
לא קשיא: הא ברטיבתא, הא ביבשתא -- the blessing is over fresh, the exemption over dry
Rava: the himalta that comes from India is permitted, and over it one says borei pri haadama
Rava (1): something is protection for the fruit only if it is there both detached and attached; the bud is there only while attached
Rava (2): something is protection for the fruit only if it is there when the fruit ripens; this bud is not
Rav and Shmuel: anything that has of the five species in it -- over it one says 'Who creates kinds of food'
had he taught only 'anything that is', I would say [mezonot] because it is in its own form, but in a mixture not; so he taught 'anything that has in it'
